steps.body: Before trusting an answer, test it against the story: totals must outgrow their parts, gaps must fit inside the longer piece, and ruler spans cannot beat their end marks.
steps.narration: Before trusting an answer, test it against the story: totals must outgrow their parts, gaps must fit inside the longer piece, and ruler spans cannot beat their end marks.

widget.prompt: A suspicious result, drawn: the 'computed gap' towers over the item it should fit inside. Which bar is longer?
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: Same start makes the compare fair — the bottom ribbon really does reach farther.

predict.prompt: A computed difference comes out LONGER than the longer object. Possible?

options.label: No — gaps fit inside the longer

predict.reveal: The difference lives inside the longer length; outgrowing it means the computation slipped.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p reasonable.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p reasonable.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: Two trail legs of 32 m and 25 m give a computed total of 30 m. Reasonable?

options.label: Impossible — a total cannot be shorter than one of its parts
options.feedback: Correct — joining 32 with anything positive lands past 32; a 30 m total contradicts its own first leg.

options.label: Reasonable — totals vary
options.feedback: Totals obey their parts: 32 + 25 must reach 57, never dip below 32.

options.label: Reasonable if the legs overlap
options.feedback: Trail legs walked one after another do not overlap — each adds its full distance.

options.label: Only a ruler could tell
options.feedback: Sense-checking needs no tools here — part-vs-total logic already rules 30 out.

commonErrors.feedback: The story has a second step — the new 30 cm still joins after the cutting.
The steps ran backward: the bow TOOK ribbon away, and the purchase brought more.
